_notes: The papal record, as data (E1 §9 A): every pope from 1939 to the last one no longer living. The game starts no earlier than 1950. After the last entry ends, popes are generated (systems/rome/papacy.ts); a living pope is never named. Dates are of the election and of the day the see fell vacant (death, or the renunciation taking effect). Temperament is the game's one axis, as it reads bishops and men (−100 traditional .. +100 progressive): a reading of emphasis, not a judgement of holiness, and flagged for review.

popes.name: Pius XII
popes.line: The last pope of the old Roman court: the war, the definition of the Assumption, and the long quiet before the Council.

popes.name: John XXIII
popes.line: The old man elected to keep the chair warm, who called the Second Vatican Council.

popes.name: Paul VI
popes.line: The pope of the Council's aftermath: the new Missal, Humanae Vitae, and the first journeys abroad.

popes.name: John Paul I
popes.line: Thirty-three days, and a smile the world remembered.

popes.name: John Paul II
popes.line: The Polish pope: twenty-six years, the fall of the Wall, the Catechism, and a hundred journeys.

popes.name: Benedict XVI
popes.line: The theologian: the encyclicals on love and hope, Summorum Pontificum, and the first renunciation in nearly six centuries.

popes.name: Francis
popes.line: The first pope from the Americas and the first Jesuit: mercy, the peripheries, synodality, and Traditionis Custodes.
